Physical AI & Robotics

NorthStar

NorthStar brings together drones, robotics and visual AI to help teams inspect physical sites, review potential issues and connect findings to project records.

Give project teams a clearer view of what is happening on site—and the context to decide what happens next.

Book a NorthStar demoSee what teams can do ↓Visit NorthStar website ↗

WHAT TEAMS CAN DO

See the site. Understand the implications.

Bring visual evidence and project information together to support inspection, coordination and review.

Inspect with better visibility.

Use drone and robotic capture to help teams review physical conditions across the areas included in an inspection. Give reviewers visual context beyond isolated notes and verbal updates.

Bring potential issues into focus.

Surface visual observations that may indicate progress, quality or safety concerns. Present the evidence clearly so qualified reviewers can investigate and decide what action is appropriate.

ILLUSTRATIVE DRAWING REFERENCEA-101 · Zone BCompare the observed slab edge with the current drawing revision before deciding on follow-up.

Connect findings to the project.

Link observations with relevant drawings and schedules so teams can understand where a finding belongs and what it may affect.

PLAN YOUR DEPLOYMENT

Start with one site. Define what success looks like.

Work with the Replaice team to identify a suitable inspection workflow, establish the evidence your teams need and plan how findings will connect to existing project processes.

INSPECTION PLANNINGSite · Evidence · ReviewDefine what to capture, the records to compare and who will decide on follow-up.

Proposed engagement approach

Scope the inspection.

Identify the site or asset, inspection objectives, capture conditions and the people responsible for reviewing findings.

Connect the right information.

Confirm which drawings, schedules and project records are available, along with access requirements and integration options.

Agree on review and evaluation.

Define how observations will be assessed, who decides on follow-up and how the initial deployment will be evaluated.
